source_text: Καὶ γὰρ ἐγώ, μαθὼν περίβλημα πονηρὸν εἰς ἀποστροφὴν τῶν ἄλλων ἀνθρώπων περιτεθειμένον ὑπὸ τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων τοῖς Χριστιανῶν θείοις διδάγμασι, καὶ ψευδολογουμένων ταῦτα καὶ τοῦ περιβλήματος κατεγέλασα καὶ τῆς παρὰ τοῖς πολλοῖς δόξης. Χριστιανὸς εὑρεθῆναι καὶ εὐχόμενος καὶ παμμάχως ἀγωνιζόμενος ὁμολογῶ, οἰχ ὅτι ἀλλότριά ἐστι τὰ Πλάτωνος διδάγματα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστι πάντη ὅμοια, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ τὰ τῶν ἄλλων, Στωϊκῶν τε καὶ ποιητῶν καὶ συγγραφέων. Ἕκαστος γάρ τις ἀπὸ μέρους τοῦ σπερματικοῦ θείου λόγου τὸ συγγενὲς ὁρῶν καλῶς ἐφθέγξατο· οἱ δὲ τἀναντία ἑαυτοῖς ἐν κυριωτέροις εἰρηκότες οὐκ ἐπιστήμην τὴν ἄπτωτον καὶ γνῶσιν τὴν ἀνέλεγκτον φαίνονται ἐσχηκέναι. Ὅσα οὖν παρὰ καλῶς εἴρηται, ἡμῶν τᾶν Χριστιανῶν ἐστι· τὸν γὰρ ἀπὸ ἀγεννήτου καὶ ἀῤῥήτου θεοῦ λόγον μετὰ τὸν θεὸν προσκυνοῦμεν καὶ ἀγαπῶμεν, ἐπειδὴ καὶ δι᾿ ἡμᾶς ἄνθρωπος γέγονεν, ὅπως καὶ τῶν παθῶν τῶν ἡμετέρων συμμέτοχος γενόμενος καὶ ἴασιν ποιήσηται. Οἱ γὰρ συγγραφεῖς πάντες διὰ τῆς ἐνούσης ἐμφύτου τοῦ λόγου σπορᾶς ἀμυδρῶς ἐδύναντο ὁρᾶν τὰ ὄντα. Ἕτερον γάρ ἐστι σπέρμα τινὸς καὶ μίμημα κατὰ δύναμιν δοθέν, καὶ ἕτερον αὐτό, οὗ κατὰ χάριν τὴν ἀπ᾿ ἐκείνου ἡ μετουσία καὶ μίμησις γίνεται.
pass_a_gloss: For I, having learned that an evil cloak has been put on the divine teachings of the Christians by the evil demons for the aversion of the other men, and these things being falsely spoken and of the cloak I laughed, and of the reputation among the many. I confess to being found a Christian and praying and struggling in every way, not because the teachings of Plato are alien to Christ, but because they are not entirely alike, just as not even the teachings of the others, of the Stoics and poets and writers, are. For each one, seeing the kinship from a part of the divine seed word, spoke well; but those who said the opposite things to themselves in the most important matters do not seem to have had untainted knowledge and unexamined understanding. Therefore, whatever has been said well is ours of the Christians; for we worship and love the Word, who is from the unbegotten and unspoken God, along with God, since He also became human for our sake, so that having become a sharer in our sufferings, He might bring about a cure. For all the writers were able to see the things that are, dimly, through the innate seed of the word that is in them. For one thing is the seed of something and an imitation given according to power, and another is the thing itself, of which the participation and imitation come according to the grace from it.

rejected: not because they are not similar

pass_b_english: I had learned that wicked demons had draped an evil cloak over the divine teachings of the Christians in order to drive other people away; when these lies about that cloak were spread, I laughed at both the falsehoods and the reputation they enjoyed among the masses.

I confess that I am found to be a Christian, and that I pray and struggle in every way, not because Plato’s teachings are alien to those of Christ, but because they are not entirely alike—just as the teachings of the Stoics, poets, and other writers are not entirely alike either.

Each person, catching sight of what is akin to them from a portion of the divine seed of the Word, spoke well as far as that went; but those who contradicted themselves on the most important matters do not appear to have possessed untainted knowledge and unassailable understanding.

Therefore, whatever has been well said belongs to us Christians; for we worship and love the Word who proceeds from the unbegotten and ineffable God, ranking Him second only to God, since He became human for our sake so that, by becoming a sharer in our sufferings, He might bring about a cure.
All the writers of old were able to perceive reality only dimly, through the innate seed of the Word implanted within them.
For a seed of something and an imitation granted according to capacity are one thing, while the thing itself—from which both participation and imitation derive by grace—is another.
